bull_bear.body: CRAR 18.46% (~Rs 1 lakh cr headroom from capital alone at ~Rs 10,000 cr per 1%). Highest-ever dividend (per prior quarter). Provisioning stance conservative: Rs 800 cr ECL buffer pre-built (outside Tier-2/PCR/profit); write-offs used to clean the book and for tax planning. Calling legacy high-cost Tier-2. No new capital raise flagged as needed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Growth gap:** deposit & overall credit growth trailing industry; CD ratio already ~86% limits headroom — funding must accelerate to sustain credit growth.
- **MSME stress:** acknowledged and "going to be there" (economy-linked); concentrated in low-ticket, guarantee-covered/state-sponsored exposures; 140-regional-office MSME customer-meet study (2,500+ MSMEs) as mitigation.
- **Maharashtra farm-loan waiver:** sizable Agri exposure; mgmt expects net-positive on reimbursement (data submitted), no impact felt yet.
- **ECL transition (1-Apr-2027):** ~Rs 6,000 cr more to provide; one-time CRAR hit to ~17.54% if fully absorbed in year one; annual run-rate credit cost still being modeled.
- **Provision/write-off optics:** NPA provision jumped to ~Rs 2,020 cr and PCR dipped — mgmt frames Q1 write-off as one-off/tax-driven, not recurring.
- Macro: Russia-Ukraine / West Asia, oil, currency, rate moves.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, granular, investor-familiar (MD engages analysts by name). Repeated "five pillars" framing (Efficiency, Robustness, Quality & Sustainable Growth, Profitability, Customer Centricity) and "business first, compliance always." Candid on the growth shortfall being a deliberate efficiency trade, and on MSME stress. Some answers meandering/verbose; several exact figures deferred ("we'll get back"). Awards cited (IIBF governance, TransUnion CIBIL data quality, IBA cybersecurity, ET Enterprise Security).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The weak headline growth is self-inflicted (bulk-deposit shedding + gold-loan de-growth ~Rs 2,500-3,000 cr + cautious CC drawdown as corporates parked ECLGS cash) — not demand loss; sets up a cleaner, higher-margin base.
- NIM guidance quietly upgraded from "defend" to "improve" — the key re-rating signal on the call.
- Rs 800 cr ECL pre-provisioning (ahead of requirement) + phaseable Rs 6,000 cr residual means the FY28 ECL cliff is largely de-risked — CRAR floor ~17.54% even in a worst-case single-year absorption.
- ECLGS uptake (~Rs 10,000 cr) is NOT a stress signal — even large corporates drew it to sit on precautionary cash; it reduced CC balances rather than funding new stress.
- PSLC (Rs 217 cr) and income-tax refund (Rs 532 cr) materially flattered fee/other income YoY — normalize when modeling.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital position at Jun-26: CRAR 18.46% and CET-I 16.38% (up 108 bps YoY), Tier II 1.14%, on Total Capital of ₹1,40,801 Cr (Tier I ₹1,32,099 Cr, Tier II ₹8,702 Cr) against RWA of ₹7,62,673 Cr; CRAR trend FY-23 16.04%, FY-24 16.97%, FY-25 18.02%, FY-26 18.10%, Q1FY27 18.46%.
- A Board Approved Capital Plan for FY27 is disclosed across Equity / AT-1 / Tier-2 with a stated Total of ₹8,000 Cr (the extract shows component figures of 3,000 and 5,000 but does not bind them unambiguously to the instruments).
- Provisioning stance is conservative: an "Other Standard Asset Provision (One-time)" of ₹700 Cr in Mar-26 and ₹100 Cr in Jun-26, with the note "Additional Provision ₹100 Cr is included in Jun-26 to strengthen the Balance Sheet" and "₹800 Crore not considered in PCR and CRAR"; PCR stands at 95.05%.
- Book Value per Share rose to ₹162.15 at Jun-26 from ₹142.37 at Jun-25, with Price to Book Value shown at 1.06 and Price to Earning at 6.17 for Jun-26 (3M).
- Instrument ratings: CRISIL AA+/Stable (AT-1) and AAA/Stable (Tier-II); ICRA AAA/Stable (Tier-II); India Ratings, CARE and Brickwork AA+/Stable and AAA/Stable; issuer ratings S&P Global BBB/Stable and Fitch BBB-/Stable.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Corporate:** self-sustained; selling (not buying) IBPC — "IBPC we do not want to even hear it." Zero-IBPC-buy policy intact.
- **RAM:** cluster scheme + Agri Unnati scheme + MSME/retail schemes to push 18-20% growth; sold good IBPC in Agri (surplus vs earlier deficit) and booked income.
- **Ecosystem banking vertical:** new sourcing engine — 1,200+ RM staff (CGM-led, 7-8 GMs, 14 DGMs), 118 centers, 12 hubs; driving CASA stickiness (95-99% in advances/SB/CA) and NACH registrations up to 18,000/day (from 12-13k).
- **Gold loan:** de-grew ~Rs 2,500-3,000 cr deliberately on compliance/regulatory tightening.
- **Treasury:** income normalized to ~Rs 630-640 cr; AFS reserve improved to -Rs 345 cr (from -Rs 800 cr).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Ownership and franchise: Govt. of India 74.76%, Public 8.63%, DII 10.79%, FII 5.82%; the deck's cover carries "Business First, Compliance Always" and a "Years of Legacy" banner.
- Pan-India distribution stated as Total Branches 8,700, Total ATMs 8,758 and Total BC Points 28,629, with branch share split Rural (30%), Semi-urban (30%), Metro (20%) and Urban (20%).
- Specialised delivery architecture: 11 LCBs & 38 MCBs, 117 Union MSME First Branches, 143 Retail Loan Points, 138 MSME Loan Points, 1,671 Gold Loan Points and 3 SAMBs & 28 ARBs; a new Ecosystem Banking Vertical is shown for acquisition of new corporate groups.
- Credit is skewed to RAM: RAM and LC & Others mix is 55 / 45 on a Global basis and 57 / 43 Domestic as at Jun-26, with Global Credit/Deposit ratio 86.10% and Domestic 83.38%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group entities] Wholly owned subsidiaries Union Bank of India (UK) Ltd., Union Asset Management Co. Pvt. Ltd. (AUM of Rs. 28,701 Crores), UBI Services Ltd. (sources retail and MSME loans for the parent), Andhra Bank Financial Services Ltd. and Union Trustee Co. Pvt. Ltd.; joint ventures Star Union Dai-ichi Life Insurance (25.10%) and ASREC India Ltd. (27.30%); associate Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank (35.00%).
- [Asset-quality clean-up] Gross NPA fell to ₹29,093 Cr / 2.65% at Jun-26 from ₹34,311 Cr / 3.52% at Jun-25 (a stated ₹12,330 Crore reduction since Jun-24 and ₹5,218 Crore since Jun-25), with Net NPA ₹5,017 Cr / 0.47%; restructuring books RF 1.0 ₹3,975 Cr and RF 2.0 ₹3,143 Cr, and SMA (>₹5 crs) total down to ₹2,382 Cr from ₹4,917 Cr.
- [Sector stress] Sectoral NPA remains concentrated in Agriculture at 7.49% (Small and Marginal Farmers 9.09%, rising through the year) and MSME at 4.15% (Micro 5.77%), versus Retail 0.89% and Large Corporates 0.99%.
- [Liquidity] Avg. LCR at 121.30% and NSFR at 118.72% as on 30.06.26; 2Y CAGR of 3.56% on both Global and Domestic Deposits.
- [Cyber security] 24*7 SOC with a Next Generation SOC, AI-led adversarial testing service provider onboarded, ASPM and CTEM, ISO 27000/29000/PCI DSS certification, cyber risk insurance, and awards including Best Security Practices in Banking Sector (DSCI 2025) and 1st Prize Advanced SOC at CII SECEX 2025.
- [Contradiction] The highlights page states Net Profit "Growth of 29.57% YoY" while the P&L statement shows Y-o-Y of 29.54% for Net Profit of ₹5,332 Cr — both readings are as printed.

latest_quarter.body: NIM 2.80% (from 2.64%) driven by: 18 bps deposit-cost reduction (bulk shed, CASA+RTD focus), re-mixing lower-yield to higher-yield advances, and LCR-guideline gains (net +2.5-3% liquidity benefit from lower run-off factors on society/trust AOP deposits). Cost of funds flat ~4.37% held up by legacy high-cost Tier-2 (some at ~9%; Rs 850 cr shed this quarter, Rs 2,500 cr call option to be exercised at ~8.7% blended). Cost-to-income down ~500 bps.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Record OP ~Rs 8,003 cr; NIM up to 2.80% (from 2.64%); ROA 1.36%; cost-to-income -500 bps; deposit cost -18 bps. Bulk deposits shed ~Rs 18-20k cr (bulk/total 27%→19%); CD ratio ~86%; CRAR 18.46%. SMA >Rs 5 cr = Rs 2,382 cr (lowest). ECL buffer Rs 800 cr (added Rs 100 cr); NPA provision ~Rs 2,020 cr; write-offs elevated (one-off). NIM guidance upgraded "defend"→"improve". FCNR USD 106 mn done (target 1.5-2 bn by Sept).
- _Q2 FY27 → check: NIM actually rising vs 2.80%; FCNR mobilization vs USD 1.5-2 bn by Sept; credit growth closing gap to industry+1% / RAM to 18-20%; deposit growth catch-up; ECL residual build (Rs 6,000 cr) pace; MSME/Maharashtra-waiver asset-quality read; PSLC run-rate vs Rs 800-900 cr FY aim; CD ratio held ≤86%._

outlook.body:
- **Credit growth:** industry + 1% (industry ~18-19%; bank currently ~13-14%); RAM (Retail/Agri/MSME) targeted >18-20%.
- **Deposit growth:** roughly credit growth minus ~2%; CASA+RTD prioritized over bulk; aspire to cut bulk deposit to ~15% of total over 1-3 years.
- **NIM:** improve from 2.80% (upgraded from "defend"); yield on advances to bottom out; deposit-cost reduction to continue.
- **FCNR / overseas:** mobilize USD 1.5-2 bn by September (~Rs 20,000 cr); USD 106 mn done; OFCB USD 200-300 mn planned.
- **Recovery:** Rs 4,500-5,000 cr for FY27 (Rs 750 cr in Q1).
- **ECLGS disbursement:** Rs 14,000-15,000 cr overall (Rs ~10,000 cr done; Rs 12,000 cr sanctioned).
- **ECL provisioning:** total requirement ~Rs 11,300-11,500 cr; carrying ~Rs 5,500 cr additional; ~Rs 6,000 cr remaining to build before the 1-Apr-2027 transition, phaseable over 4 years.
- **PSLC fee:** Rs 800-900 cr full-year aspiration (conditional on Agri/SMF growth).
- **CD ratio:** hold ~85-86%, not much beyond.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Corporate pipeline: >Rs 1,00,000 cr sanctioned but undisbursed, drawing down in stages; ~Rs 60,000-70,000 cr underwritten over the last 8-9 months and being down-sold. Domestic corporate:RAM mix ~57:43. Liquidity: LCR 121% (board floor 107%, RBI 100%) — ~Rs 42,000 cr surplus (1 bp ≈ Rs 2,000 cr); NSFR comfortable. Deposits taken Rs 30,000-40,000 cr in the quarter despite bulk shedding; CASA avg Rs 24,000+ cr, RTD avg Rs 17,000 cr (total Rs 41,000 cr average build Mar→Jun).
